title: ₹1 Crore Ka Flat Bika: Builder Ke Paas Kitna Bacha?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. The home loan reels cover the buyer's side, and this is the seller's side, which people almost never see. Real estate is the most universal aspiration for this audience, and listed developers like DLF and Godrej Properties publish margins, so the numbers are researchable.
text:
**HISAAB FACT SHEET: Where the ₹1 crore of a new flat goes**

Date of research: 9 Nov 2026. Figures are the latest I found, mostly FY26 (year to Mar 2026).

**0. Two things to fix before scripting**
- No source gives a clean split of ₹1 crore into land, construction, approvals, marketing, finance and profit. Each source gives a range for one bucket, and the ranges don't add to 100%. Label the bar "typical ranges, varies by city and project".
- GST and stamp duty are not inside the ₹1 crore sticker price. The buyer pays them on top. Square Yards says the total cost of buying a flat is typically 7 to 12 percent higher than the quoted price. [https://www.squareyards.com/blog/total-cost-of-buying-a-flat]
- Square Yards puts statutory charges (stamp duty, registration, GST) at 5 to 8% of base price. [https://www.squareyards.com/blog/total-cost-of-buying-a-flat]
- Suggested structure: Bar 1 is what the buyer pays (₹1 crore plus tax). Bar 2 is where the builder's ₹1 crore goes.

**1. Bar 2: builder's cost buckets (ranges from sources)**

Land
- Equirus (investment bank) says land is 20–30 per cent of an average project's cost structure. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/industry/news/real-estate-developers-stuck-between-construction-cost-wall-and-soft-market-125051100698_1.html]
- Another guide says land is 20–35% of project revenue in metros. In Tier-2 cities, land can be as low as 12–15% of project cost. [https://realtypromoo.com/guides/what-are-the-profit-margins-of-branded-developers-in-india-an-insight]
- That second source is a lower-authority blog. Treat it as indicative.

Construction
- Equirus says construction is around 40 per cent of an average project. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/industry/news/real-estate-developers-stuck-between-construction-cost-wall-and-soft-market-125051100698_1.html]
- Another guide gives 25–40% of total project cost. [https://realtypromoo.com/guides/what-are-the-profit-margins-of-branded-developers-in-india-an-insight]
- Colliers says average residential construction cost rose from ₹2,000 per sq ft in October 2020 to ₹2,800–2,850 per sq ft in March 2025. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/industry/news/real-estate-developers-stuck-between-construction-cost-wall-and-soft-market-125051100698_1.html]

Approvals, FSI premiums and regulatory costs
- A guide puts this at 5–10%, including RERA registration, FSI premiums, development charges, and stamp duty on land purchase. [https://realtypromoo.com/guides/what-are-the-profit-margins-of-branded-developers-in-india-an-insight]
- In Mumbai the premium can be far bigger. In 2021, FSI premiums/fungible FSI and other concessions accounted for 25-33 per cent of overall project cost (including land). That is an older figure (2021) and Mumbai-specific. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/economy-policy/maharashtra-move-to-cut-construction-premiums-to-lower-project-costs-by-17-121010700970_1.html]
- Sunteck's chairman said developers can go up to 5-6 FSI from a base of 1.33 in Mumbai city and 1 in the suburbs by paying premiums. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/economy-policy/maharashtra-move-to-cut-construction-premiums-to-lower-project-costs-by-17-121010700970_1.html]

Marketing and broker fees
- On a new project the builder pays the broker. The builder pays the broker a commission, usually between 1% and 3%. The buyer pays 0%. [https://www.merawazood.com/blog/real-estate/real-estate-broker-commission-rates]
- Exclusive developer mandates pay typically higher, 2-4%. [https://remax.in/blog/how-real-estate-brokerage-works-in-india-2026-guide-20]
- On ₹1 crore, 1–3% works out to ₹1–3 lakh (my arithmetic on the sourced percentage).
- I found no sourced figure for total ad and marketing spend as a % of sales. Don't state one.

Finance cost
- I found no sourced finance-cost % of project cost for Indian residential projects. Don't state one.
- Listed developers are now lightly indebted. Anarock says the average net debt-to-equity of top listed developers fell to a historic low of 0.05 in FY25, down from 0.55 at the FY17 peak. [https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/top-developers-pre-sales-targets-fy26-anarock-dlf-prestige-real-estate-125090100493_1.html]
- DLF has zero gross debt in its development business and a net cash surplus of ₹14,155 crore. [https://www.dlf.in/media-press-release/dlf_q4_and_fy26_press_release.pdf]
- Definition note: Godrej's "Adjusted EBITDA" is EBITDA plus interest included in cost of sale. So some interest sits inside project cost and gets added back. [https://gplwebsitecdnblob.blob.core.windows.net/godrej-cdn/Files/s-efinal-ip-cmhn2rofo0000q3ph9gs6ccbv.pdf]

Builder margin (the payoff). The Equirus view is EBITDA margin hovers around 30 per cent. [https://www.business-standard.com/amp/industry/news/real-estate-developers-stuck-between-construction-cost-wall-and-soft-market-125051100698_1.html]
